sentences.text: The holotype — the specimen the species is based on — includes a left humerus measuring 123 centimeters in length, suggesting the animal reached an estimated total length of 11 meters.
This dinosaur is very similar to Aeolosaurus, differing only in specific vertebral details.
Jorge Orlando Calvo and Juan Domingo Porfiri named Panamericansaurus schroederi in 2010, honoring the Pan American Energy company and the Schroeder family who owned the land.
The fossils were found in June 2003 in the Allen Formation near San Patricio del Chañar, Neuquén, Argentina.
It belongs to the clade Aeolosaurini of the family Titanosauridae, alongside Aeolosaurus and Gondwanatitan.
Panamericansaurus lived between 75 and 70 million years ago during the Campanian and Maastrichtian stages, with a specific time range from 72.2 to 66 million years ago in what is now South America.
